# vergeio_vm_import (Resource)

`vergeio_vm_import` declares an image the rest of the configuration depends on.

`target = "vm"` (the default) imports an OVA or OVF through `vm_imports` and waits until VergeOS reports `complete` or `warning`. Set one of `file`, `url`, `volume`, or `shared_object`. `file` is a media-catalog file that is already on the system. `url` is downloaded into the catalog first. `volume` is a NAS volume key, and `volume_path` is the OVA or OVF on that volume. A failed import returns as soon as VergeOS reports `error` or `aborted`. It does not sit through `timeouts.create`.

VergeOS rejects a bare disk image on `vm_imports` (`qcow2`, `qcow`, `vmdk`, `vhd`, `vhdx`, `raw`, `img`, `vdi`, `iso`) with "Unknown Import file type". Set `target = "media"` for those files. Create downloads the URL into the media catalog and waits until the file has a size. `file_id` is the id `vergeio_mediasources` lists and the id `vergeio_vm_drive.media_source` uses with `media = "import"`.

Destroy removes the import row and the VM this resource created, unless `delete_vm` is false. An import that adopted a VM which already existed (`adopted`) deletes neither the VM nor the `vm_imports` row. The resource that created the VM still tracks that row. Destroy of the creating resource removes the row and, unless `delete_vm` is false, the VM. It removes a catalog file this resource downloaded when `delete_file` is true. A file passed in `file` is left in place. A media import is the file, and destroy always removes it.

`terraform import` reads `file`, `volume`, `volume_path`, `shared_object`, and the preserve, tier, and interface options from the `vm_imports` row. `url` is not a column on that row. `files.url` is an argument VergeOS does not return, so a download writes the address on the next line of the catalog file description (`Downloaded for VM import <name>` or `Downloaded for media import <name>`). Import reads that line, sets `url`, and sets `owns_file`. A download created before that line was written has no copy of the address that VergeOS returns, and import of that file still has no `url`. `file_name` is not a column and is not restored. Create stores each option VergeOS saved, including a platform default the configuration left out. A later refresh does the same for a state that still has the option null. An omitted option keeps that stored value. Setting the configuration to the stored value does not replace the VM. Changing a stored value replaces the import. `terraform plan -generate-config-out` writes that source.

`preserve_bios_serial`, `guest_agent_preinstalled`, and `replicate_tags` are VergeOS 26.2 columns. On an older system they stay at the configured value because the API does not return them. `url` is stored in state and on the catalog file description. Do not put a credential in it.

An import that is already running in the UI or in Ansible is [`vergeio_vm_import`](../data-sources/vm_import.html) (data source). The volume export configuration is [`vergeio_vm_export`](vm_export.html). Starting an export, and the migration procedure around it, stays in the Ansible collection. See [VM import and migration](../guides/vm-import.html).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Import an OVA as a virtual machine. Create waits until VergeOS
# reports complete or warning. A failed import returns immediately.
# Destroy removes the import row and the VM it created.

resource "vergeio_vm_import" "example" {
  name           = "imported-guest"
  url            = "https://downloads.example.com/images/guest.ova"
  preserve_macs  = false
  preferred_tier = "3"

  timeouts {
    create = "20m"
  }
}
```

```terraform
# Download a disk image into the media catalog. VergeOS rejects this
# file on vm_imports. Attach it with vergeio_vm_drive media = "import".

resource "vergeio_vm_import" "disk" {
  name      = "golden"
  target    = "media"
  url       = "https://downloads.example.com/images/golden.qcow2"
  file_name = "golden.qcow2"

  timeouts {
    create = "20m"
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) VM name to create, or the catalog file name when target is media and file_name is omitted. Changing it replaces the import.

### Optional

- `delete_file` (Boolean) Destroy deletes the catalog file downloaded from url for a VM import. A file passed in file is left in place. Defaults to true. A media import is the file, and destroy always removes it.
- `delete_vm` (Boolean) Destroy deletes the VM this import created. A VM that already had this name is left in place. Defaults to true. Has no effect when target is media.
- `file` (Number) Media-catalog file id of an OVA or OVF that is already on VergeOS. Import reads this from the vm_imports file column. Changing it replaces the import.
- `file_name` (String) Catalog name for the file downloaded from url. The default for a VM import is the URL's file name. The default for a media import is name. vm_imports has no file_name column, and import does not restore it. Changing it replaces the import.
- `guest_agent_preinstalled` (Boolean) Mark the guest agent as already installed. VergeOS 26.2. Omit on create to leave the platform default. Create and import store the value VergeOS saved. An omitted value keeps the stored value. Setting the configuration to that stored value does not replace the import. Changing a stored value replaces the import.
- `no_optical_drives` (Boolean) Skip optical drives from an OVA. Omit on create to leave the platform default. Create and import store the value VergeOS saved. An omitted value keeps the stored value. Setting the configuration to that stored value does not replace the import. Changing a stored value replaces the import.
- `override_drive_interface` (String) Drive interface to use instead of the source interface. default leaves the source value. Create and import store the value VergeOS saved. An omitted value keeps the stored value. Setting the configuration to that stored value does not replace the import. Changing a stored value replaces the import.
- `override_nic_interface` (String) NIC interface to use instead of the source interface. default leaves the source value. Create and import store the value VergeOS saved. An omitted value keeps the stored value. Setting the configuration to that stored value does not replace the import. Changing a stored value replaces the import.
- `preferred_tier` (String) Storage tier, from 1 through 5. Omit on create to leave the platform default. Create and import store the value VergeOS saved. An omitted value keeps the stored value. Setting the configuration to that stored value does not replace the import. Changing a stored value replaces the import.
- `preserve_bios_serial` (Boolean) Keep the source SMBIOS serial. VergeOS 26.2. Omit on create to leave the platform default. Create and import store the value VergeOS saved. An omitted value keeps the stored value. Setting the configuration to that stored value does not replace the import. Changing a stored value replaces the import.
- `preserve_drive_format` (Boolean) Keep the source disk format. Omit on create to leave the platform default. Create and import store the value VergeOS saved. An omitted value keeps the stored value. Setting the configuration to that stored value does not replace the import. Changing a stored value replaces the import.
- `preserve_macs` (Boolean) Keep source MAC addresses. Omit on create to leave the platform default. Create and import store the value VergeOS saved. An omitted value keeps the stored value. Setting the configuration to that stored value does not replace the import. Changing a stored value replaces the import.
- `replicate_tags` (Boolean) Copy VMware tags and categories onto the imported VM. VergeOS 26.2. Omit on create to leave the platform default. Create and import store the value VergeOS saved. An omitted value keeps the stored value. Setting the configuration to that stored value does not replace the import. Changing a stored value replaces the import.
- `shared_object` (Number) Shared-object id for a tenant import. Import reads this from the vm_imports row. Changing it replaces the import.
- `target` (String) vm imports an OVA or OVF as a virtual machine. media downloads a disk image into the media catalog. Defaults to vm. Changing it replaces the import.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) How long create waits for the import or the catalog download, and how long destroy waits for a guest to stop. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `url` (String) http or https address of an OVA, OVF, or disk image. VergeOS downloads it into the media catalog. The address is stored in state and on the next line of the catalog file description, because files.url is not returned. Import reads that line. Changing it replaces the import. Do not put a credential in it.
- `volume` (String) NAS volume key, a 40 character hex string, that holds the OVA or OVF. Import reads this from the vm_imports row. Changing it replaces the import.
- `volume_path` (String) Path of the OVA or OVF on volume. When volume is set, create and import store the vm_imports value. An omitted value keeps the stored value. Setting the configuration to that stored value does not replace the import. Changing a stored value replaces the import.

### Read-Only

- `aborted` (Boolean) True when the import was aborted.
- `adopted` (Boolean) True when a VM with this name already existed and no new import was posted. Destroy does not delete that VM or the vm_imports row. The resource that created the VM still tracks the row.
- `failed_drive_count` (Number) How many drives VergeOS has already failed.
- `file_id` (Number) Media-catalog file id used for the import. For target media this is the file the resource created.
- `id` (String) vm_imports key, a 40 character hex string, or the media file id when target is media.
- `importing` (Boolean) True while VergeOS is still importing.
- `owns_file` (Boolean) True when this resource downloaded the catalog file and delete_file may remove it.
- `status` (String) Import status: initializing, importing, complete, aborted, error, or warning. A media file is complete once it has a size.
- `status_info` (String) Detail VergeOS reported for status.
- `uuid` (String) Source VM UUID reported by VergeOS.
- `vm_id` (Number) Key of the VM the import created. Null for a media file, and null until VergeOS assigns one.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) How long create waits. A duration such as "20m". Defaults to 10m. A failed import returns as soon as VergeOS reports it.
- `delete` (String) How long destroy waits after one ACPI poweroff before killing the VM. A duration such as "2m". Defaults to 2m.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The `terraform import` command can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import vergeio_vm_import.example <vm_imports_key>
```
